A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 53-page versions of the same DataMan study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D are readable and directly matchable.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, perplexity and downstream-task results, instruction-following evaluations, and DataMan accuracy and corpus analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices B-C, including experiments with 30B and 60B training tokens.

M1.justification: The quality criteria, domain recognition, pointwise annotation, DataMan training objectives, and source/domain-aware sampling procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The training corpora, ten downstream tasks, instruction-following evaluation, and medicine, law, and finance evaluations are retained. Removing the Other-source statistic from Table 6 does not establish a coverage removal: Appendix B.1 still explicitly describes including that data.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Uniform, DSIR with Wiki/Book, perplexity filtering, and Qurating criteria and their mixture. Uniform +50% data is relocated within tables, not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 changes the reported fine-tuning dataset size from 35.7k to 357k documents. This localized correction agrees with Table 6 and Appendix B.2 already present in v1, although Section 3.4 still says 35,700. It does not establish an actual tenfold expansion or rerun; other settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 revises the BoolQ evidence in the analysis of perplexity versus ICL performance by correcting plotted baseline points and correlations. Other quality-rating, misclassification, and raw-document analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Seed information, human-rating reliability procedures, and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Figure 6 retains Pearson and Spearman correlations; changed coefficient values are result corrections.

E6.justification: Figure 6 corrects BoolQ baseline points, including DSIR with Book from approximately 61.4 to 57.9, matching unchanged Table 14. Pearson r changes from -0.46 to -0.42 and Spearman rho from -0.03 to -0.09. Table 6 removes the Other-source entry of 67,865 documents (19.05%). Benchmark table scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The annotation definitions, pointwise-loss/ranking-error bound, NDCG formulation, and sampling equations are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about DataMan, its quality criteria, domain mixing, and model performance. Specifying l=5 in the instruction-following discussion clarifies an existing claim.

C2.justification: Appendix C narrows its description of long-tail domain proportions from having fallen to their lowest levels to remaining at the lowest levels. Mechanism explanations, applicability discussions, and stated limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 revises the documented dataset size, while Table 6 loses the exact Other-source breakdown despite retaining the adjacent 19% description. Hyperparameters, hardware, training details, release statements, and link targets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work discussions, cited works, references, and positioning relative to prior data-selection methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and terminology edits, including specifying Overall Score l=5 and refining the DataPajama description. Section order, narrative structure, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 12-14 move Uniform +50% data into the Uniform block. Figure 6 revises its BoolQ scatter and clarifies legend labels; Table 6 replaces the Other-source entry with dashes. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Figure 6's BoolQ baseline points to agree with Table 14 and improves legend labels and baseline grouping. Appendix B.1's dataset count also better matches existing tabulated information. These accuracy and clarity gains are limited by the unchanged 35,700 count in Section 3.4 and the loss of the Other-source breakdown in Table 6; the scientific method and principal evidence remain stable.
